```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Distribution fits a 90-day goal better. B sells through the Shopify App Store, where merchants already shop for apps and ads start at $5/day, with one reported install cost about 1/3 of other ad networks. A's main channel is SEO/content, with a cited 7-month payback. That is a poor match for getting a paying customer inside 90 days, and A's community channel has no cost estimate [unsourced].",
    "B's incumbents look weak and beatable. Describly has 1 review, a 1-star complaint that it 'stopped working'. Descrii has 0 reviews and Gelo.ai has 3. In A, Prerender.io has operated since 2014 with 72+ G2 reviews, and competitors span $5/mo to enterprise, so there is little room on price or trust.",
    "B has a clear, sourced wedge. Free Shopify Magic covers basic descriptions but explicitly lacks alt text, image input, titles and bulk editing, which is exactly what B adds. A has no comparable gap. Its stated pivot, AI-crawler visibility, is only an open question.",
    "A faces a sourced, structural headwind. Google's own documentation calls dynamic rendering a workaround rather than a long-term solution and steers developers to SSR/SSG frameworks. A's addressable market likely shrinks over time, and A also carries cloaking-policy support risk.",
    "B's demand evidence is easier to verify. Its Reddit quotes carry direct URLs. A's Reddit quotes are cited only by subreddit and year, with no links, and A's one named customer quote is a vendor testimonial.",
    "B has real weaknesses, which keep this from being a clear win. Its price point is low ($12–19 entry), retention risk is real because a catalog may only need processing once, and the ADA settlement figures come from vendor-adjacent blogs. These hurt long-term revenue more than they hurt the odds of a first paying customer."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence and its viability claim. The Reddit quotes have no URLs, so they cannot be verified. The only named customer quote is a testimonial on Prerender.io's own pricing page. The Case For says 'several thin competitors already run this model profitably at small scale', but the brief gives no source for anyone's profitability.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both ideas are crowded, commoditized categories, and neither brief offers a validated differentiator or any direct evidence of willingness to pay beyond competitor list prices. B wins mainly on a faster path to a customer through the App Store and weaker incumbents, not on proven economics. B's brief also lists Descrii as 'launched July 2026', which looks like a data error and slightly lowers trust in that competitor detail. A could do better if its higher price point and the AI-crawler angle proved real, but neither brief provides evidence for that."
}
```
